To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
COSMIC GPS RO temperature profiles in clouds are significantly warmer than those of the ECMWF and NCEP–NCAT reanalysis and that a new cloudy retrieval scheme is proposed to correct this bias.

COSMIC GPS RO temperature data are systematically biased with respect to the NCEP–NCER and ECMWF analyses, and this bias is opposite for cloudy and clear-skiy conditions, and that the new cloudy retrieval algorithm improves the agreement between COSMIC GPS RO and the NCEP reanalysis and ECMW analyses in cloudy conditions.

1) a new COSMIC GPS RO temperature retrieval algorithm for cloudy conditions is proposed and validated, and 2) the new algorithm is able to improve the accuracy of the retrieved COSMIC RO temperature in clouds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of GPS radio occultation data to retrieve thermodynamic profiles of clouds.
the use of GPS RO data to retrieve thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere in cloudy conditions.
the development of an improved GPS RO cloudy-sky retrieval algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new COSMIC GPS RO data are not affected significantly by clouds and can be used to study clouds on a global scale.
the GPS RO temperature data are more accurate than the NCEP–NCar or ECMWF analyses in clouds.
the GPS RO temperature profiles in clouds are more likely to be biased high than those in clear air.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to use GPS RO data for profiling cloud thermodynamic states on a global basis and to improve the global analysis and forecast models by assimilating the GPS RO data with the new cloudy retrieval algorithm.
the COSMIC GPS RO temperature profiles in clouds are not only of high quality but also of high value to climate and weather research.

the GPS RO data have been used to study the cloud properties, such as cloud height, liquid water content (LWC), ice water content (IWC), cloud top pressure and temperature, cloud optical depth (COD), and the cloud fraction, and that the GPS RO temperature profiles in clouds are useful for the validation of the global reanalysis and analysis products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the COSMIC GPS RO observations are useful for studying clouds.
COSMIC GPS RO data can be used to study cloud properties and thermodynamic states within clouds.
GPS RO observations can be used to detect the cloud thermodynamics, and thus can be used to study the physical processes in clouds.
